My husband has been on medication long term ie since the 1990’s therefore I believe I know what I am talking about.

Anyway apart from the fact that in April 2024 he was hospitalized for a month and then had to attend hospital daily for 6 weeks to enable him to get intravenous medication, and even after that spent another few months on various medication until he was pretty much fully recovered.
It is now very important to me that he gets his medication on time!
Fair comment I’d expect but I have in the last 18 months especially (or maybe I’ve only noticed due to the severity of his latest illness) noticed that the system does not work!
Used to be I ordered them on my phone ( his meds) repeatedly this did not work, I have for maybe 6 months now had to revert to “old school” and write on a chatty what is required and yet again I have lost count of the amount of times the script does not reach the chemist!
To add insult to injury..I complained and then basically because I did I was threatened with being excluded from the practice! Okay I was a bit upset at the time but I did NOT shout at the receptionist nor did I behave in.a threatening manner!
I explained in no uncertain terms that I am not happy about being mucked about 1 I do not have the time and 2 I do not want to see my husband that I’ll ever again, during the first week they were not sure he would survive and all this is down to not very good medical practice in the first place as in someone who is allegedly medically qualified should have realised that the diclofenac they put him on should have been stopped and not allowed to burn a hole in his colon and therefore allow bacteria to seep through to his peritoneal and allow 4 abcesses to grow and nearly kill him.
To say I am not impressed is an understatement I am still awaiting a reply to my letter which was sent in before the end of November and yet it is still happening, no prescription- not ordered this is twice this week alone and I can assure you they were ordered.
Does anyone have any suggestions on how to get prescribed medicine or should I consult a solicitor on what I have just realised might be a malpractice
